newsitem.title: GERMANY: Turkish children protest against German law.
newsitem.headline: Turkish children protest against German law.

text.p: Around 100 Turkish children stayed away from school in Hamburg on Thursday, forming a human chain around a city centre church to protest against a new law which obliges them to hold residence permits.
The children, many carrying banners protesting against the new law, and their parents staged the demonstration at the city's St Michaelis church.
Under a rule which came into force last month, children under 16 from Turkey, Tunisia, Morocco and former Yugoslavia now have to apply for visas to visit relatives in Germany.
The 2.2 million members of Germany's Turkish community do not have German citizenship, meaning their children now have to apply as "foreigners" for residence permits.
The government insists the measure became necessary because foreigners were abusing its previously relaxed stance on children visiting relatives in Germany by staying permanently.
Turkish communities in Berlin and Frankfurt were also due to protest against the law later on Thursday.
